10.HEMOPHILIA
•X – linked recessive disorders:
-Type A – Absent or reduced Factor VIII.
-Type B – Absent or reduced Factor IX.
•Male affected 50%. If female
•Female carrier 50%. is carrier
-50% has no previous history
-Spontaneous mutation in 40 – 50% cases
-More mutations in spermatogenesis than oogenesis
-In maternal Grand Father.
•Factor VIII: VWF <0.7 is suggestive of carriership

Types:

1.Mild: .06 – 0.40IU/ml bleeding after
2.Mod: 0.01 – 0.5 trauma
3.Severe: < 0.01 – spontaneous bleeding in Joints and muscles.

Carriers: risk of bleeding during invasive procedures, TOP, C/S, SVD when levels between 0.4 – 0.6.

Neonates: Male at risk of ICH, ECH, iatrogenic haemorrhage.

Pre – Pregnancy Management:

•Monitor levels before pregnancy.
•Correct weight and iron deficiency => ed bleeding risk.
•Genetic counselling + genetic testing of partner.
•Written informed consent before genetic Testing.

ANC:

•MDT management of pregnancy
•Prenatal diagnosis – all carriers of severe hemophilia
-9 weeks CFFDNA in all pts to determine sex.
-If male fetus then determine hemophilia status by

1.CVS at 11 – 14 weeks.

2.Amniocentesis in 3rd

•Male fetus – informed choices.
•If PND not performed – consider as affected fetus.
•Factor levels:
-Check at booking, before invasive procedure and in 3rd -( Target – 0.5I/ml)
-If treatment is given then target is 1U/ml.
-MDT includes neonatologist and obstetrician.

Acute Bleeding:

•Tranexamic acid all women
-In combination of factor VIII if levels are < 0.5.
-Solely if > 0.5.

in all procedures until Bleeding settles.

Desmopressin (DDAVP):

•DDAVP level VIII but not IX via V2 receptors on endothelial cells.
-Used in labor to levels of factor VIII
-S/C or I/V 0.3ug/kg, Repeat 12 – 24hrs, Risk of tachyphylaxis.
-Avoid in HTN, pre – eclampsia.
•Antidiuretic effect => hyponatremia – fits.
•Fluid restriction to 1 lit/day/
•Electrolyte monitoring.
•Level monitoring before and after treatment.

r Factor VIII:

•If DDVAP not effective, monitor levels before, after and 4 – 6 hours after infusion.

 

 

Intrapartum Care Plan:

•Written/ documented in advance of 37 weeks.
•Anesthesia evaluation, Neonatologist informed.
•ECV in Male not recommended.
•In female ECV can be done.
•Gender not known – avoid ECV.

IPC:

•MOD discussed in MDT – target levels >1 IU/ml
•affected Male Fetus/ unknown status.

Elective C section @ 39 weeks with a clear Plan in case of spontaneous labor.

Consider Maternal Bleeding risks.

 

•Female gender or unaffected male
•Vaginal delivery: spontaneous labor is preferred.

IOL if concerns regarding travel to specialist center.

•2nd Stage: Plan documented, involving senior obstetrician.
•Avoid midcavity forceps, ventouse, FBS scalp Electrodes, Outlet or low Forceps can be used.

No Measures in case of Female fetus.

•ICH more in Pre – Term Babies.

Analgesics/ Anaesthesia:

•Regional Anaesthesia (target > 0.5IU/ml) Neuraxial Hematoma – Neurological injury.
•I/M injections avoided if levels < 0.5IU/ml.
•Anaesthesia evaluation by senior Anaesthetist @ 32 – 34 weeks after knowledge of VIII/IX levels.

Haemostatic Management during labor/ Delivery:

⇨Levels < 0.5IU/ml -> treatment:
-DDAVP to VIII.
-Factor IX concentrate.

Targets 1 IU/ml.

⇨Tranexamic Acid:
-Solely in low normal levels.
-In combination with factor in low levels.

Treatment as close as labor.

Post partum care:

•Active 3rd stage of labour.
•Maintain levels after labour
-3 days after SVD.
-5 days after C/S.
•Tranexamic acid till lochia is minimal (21 – 58days carrier).
•Thromboprophylaxis avoided if level < 06, use UfH If it is required.

PPH prophylaxis:

•Tranexamic acid 1g three times a day for 7 – 14 days (all Pts).

Neonatal Management:

•Cord blood sampling – results interpreted against age – adjusted ranges.
•Repeat testing 3 – 6m0 of age in mild cases.
•Oral vitamin K. affected
•Cranial USG neonates.

MRI Skull – if S/S of ICH or ICH on USG.

•Short term P0 prophylaxis – severe/ Moderate cases with traumatic delivery, Pre – Term birth and @ ed risk of bleeding.

Female Baby => No testing required.

Target Levels:

•Antenatal = > 0.5
•Treatment given > 1.
•I/P >1.
•Procedures = > 0.5.
•PP = > 0.5.
•VTE prophylaxis > 0.6.
•I/M injections > 0.5/
•Regional Anaesthesia > 0.5

Fetal Effects of Hemophilia:

•Genetic Transmission.
•ICH.
•ECH.

Maternal Effects of Hemophilia:

1.Risk of bleeding.
2.PPH
3.APH
4.Muscle and joint Bleeding is the Hallmark of Hemophilia.
